does: Beats tahini with lemon juice and cold water into a pale, smooth, pourable sauce. The paste stiffens and looks curdled when the first liquid goes in, then turns silky and loose as more water is beaten in.
how: Stir the tahini well first, as its oil rises to the top. If garlic is used, crush it with salt and stir it into the lemon juice.
Put the tahini in a bowl and stir in the lemon juice. The paste will seize and thicken, as it should.
Add cold water a spoonful at a time, beating hard after each, until the paste loosens, lightens and turns smooth.
Stop at the texture the dish wants: thick as cream for a dip, thinner for pouring over fish or falafel.
Taste, and adjust the lemon juice and the salt.

cues.text: A pale, creamy, glossy sauce with no oil standing on top.
Stiff and tight after the lemon juice goes in, then silky and easy to stir as the water goes in.
Nutty and tart, with no bitter edge.

mistakes.mistake: Pouring in all the water at once, so that the sauce splits into oil and a watery paste.
mistakes.fix: Add it a spoonful at a time and beat after each.

mistakes.mistake: Giving up when the paste seizes, thinking it has gone wrong.
mistakes.fix: Keep beating and keep adding water. It loosens.

mistakes.mistake: Using tahini from the top of the jar, where the oil has risen, so that the sauce is thin and oily.
mistakes.fix: Stir the jar well before measuring.

comes_after.why: The sauce is beaten by hand until smooth, so a steady beating hand comes first.

variant_of.differs: No oil is added. The oil already in the tahini is spread through lemon juice and water by beating, and the paste first seizes and then loosens.
